title: Timing for Initial Medicare Enrollment & Subsequent Changes
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4
question_text: When can I select my Medicare coverage plan, and when can I change it later?

accurate_complete: Mentioned that you can enroll in Medicare / select coverage within 3 months of turning 65 (Initial Enrollment Period)
Substantively answered the 'when can I change it' question by referencing the Open Enrollment Period, Annual Election Period, or Special Enrollment Periods
accurate_incomplete: Some substantive information was provided but both components of the question were not answered
Said shopper can enroll 'now' (because within 3 months of turning 65) but did not address when changes can be made
not_substantive: Counselor did not answer the question
Declined to answer without shopper's Medicare card
incorrect: Incorrect information was provided that was substantive enough to materially change the substance of the answer or affect an enrollee's decision (e.g., wrong enrollment window dates, stated cannot change plans)

scoring_notes: Score as Accurate and Complete only if BOTH components are addressed: (1) enrollment timing near age 65, AND (2) at least one annual change period. Score as Accurate but Incomplete if only one component is addressed. The materiality standard applies to Incorrect: minor wording imprecision (e.g., saying 'within 3 months' vs the full 7-month IEP window) does not automatically trigger Incorrect.
